headline: The Texas grid operator's April forecast said power demand could more than quadruple by 2032, mainly because of data centers, though it admits the figure is probably too high.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 3: the forecast dates from mid-April 2026, so this is old news re-dated by a late repost.
importance_line: Texas electricity users and regulators plan around these numbers, and the forecast shows how many data-center requests are queuing for power, but ERCOT itself says the figure is probably too high.
summary: AI News Desk reports, from the San Antonio Express-News and Houston Public Media, that ERCOT, the operator of the Texas power grid, forecast in April that peak demand could reach more than four times today's record by 2032, with data centers the largest source of growth. ERCOT then told the state regulator the figure is likely an overestimate because it is built on utilities' reports of proposed large users, and it plans to revise it.
notes: Pool source EnergyNow.com not readable; same-forecast coverage by San Antonio Express-News (16 Apr) and Houston Public Media (22 Apr) used. Old news re-dated.
